messages:
emma-partnerships: Heads up — NovaCloud's PO failed to publish in the marketplace portal this morning. Partner says the portal rejects the uploaded PO PDF with an 'invalid signer format' error. We're blocked from creating the private offer :grimacing:

devin-legal: Can you paste the exact portal error and the PO metadata they sent? Sometimes the portal enforces a signer object with name+email instead of a free-form signature line.

emma-partnerships: Error text from portal screenshot: `400 Bad Request — invalid_signer_format: expected {"name":string,"email":string} got string`. PO filename: "NovaCloud_PO_6789.pdf". Customer procurement insists on our signed PO for their internal routing.

maria-sales: Customer timeline is tight — they need the private offer created before EOD to close the quarter. Is there a quick workaround? Could partner upload a JSON metadata file or is there a portal setting? @suresh-ops any suggestions?

suresh-ops: The portal API accepts a signer JSON in the metadata payload. Normally our reseller flow wraps the PO and injects signer metadata, but NovaCloud used a third-party procurement system that flattened the signer into the PDF text. We can either: 1) ask the partner to resubmit with a signer field in the portal UI, or 2) we upload via API and attach a small metadata JSON alongside the PDF. The problem: their finance team only accepts an "Executed PO" PDF; adding a separate metadata file might fail their audit.

alex-eng: Quick hack: we can call the portal POST /offers endpoint and send multipart with fields: `file=@po.pdf` and `signer={"name":"Jane Doe","email":"jane@novacloud.com"}`. I tested with a staging token — portal accepts it. Need someone with access to the partner's final PDF and approval from legal to assert signer identity.

devin-legal: We can't fabricate signer info. If partner confirms the signer and provides a cover email from the signer address, legal can approve attaching the signer JSON. Also need to make sure EULA redlines are not part of this flow — NovaCloud earlier sent a one-line redline to section 6.2 (audit clause). That needs sign-off separately; it shouldn't block the PO upload if the PO is the only hurdle.

emma-partnerships: I just checked with NovaCloud — their procurement lead (jane@novacloud.com) can send a confirmation email. I'll ask them to send the signed PDF and a separate confirmation email from the signer address right now. If they do, who can run the API upload?

maria-sales: I can run it if legal confirms it's OK. I'm in touch with the customer on the confirmation email.

devin-legal: Once we have the confirmation email, I'm good to approve the API attach workflow. Also loop in Marketplace ops for audit retention so we keep the email in the offer record.

marketplace-bot: [deploy-notice] New portal upload endpoint rate limits: 120/minute for partner orgs. No current incidents.

emma-partnerships: Action items: 1) NovaCloud to send signed PDF + confirmation from signer (Emma) 2) Maria to upload via API (Maria) 3) Devin to confirm legal approval once email received (Devin) 4) Suresh to monitor portal upload and confirm offer creation (Suresh). I'll update here when the email arrives. :thumbsup:

maria-sales: Got the confirmation email from jane@novacloud.com. Uploading now and will paste API response here.

alex-eng: FYI, if upload fails with a 409 it's usually because the partner org mapping uses a different vendor alias. We had a similar hit last quarter; we can map alias on our side but that requires Marketplace admin privileges.

maria-sales: Upload response: `201 Created` — offer id `off_32a9f`. Private offer created. Adding NovaCloud's billing entity now.

suresh-ops: I see `off_32a9f` in the console, status: awaiting-billing-entity. Sending mapping request to marketplace admin to clear the alias mismatch.

devin-legal: Confirmed legal sign-off on using the confirmation email as signer proof. Proceed with offer publication.

emma-partnerships: Closing the loop: private offer published and customer confirmed receipt. Notes for next time: add a KB entry for partner procurement teams on required signer metadata format, and flag common procurement systems that flatten signer fields. Great work team :tada:
